name: Ontario
note: In Ontario the funeral director registers the death. The certifier (physician, nurse practitioner, registered nurse for expected deaths, or coroner) delivers the medical certificate to the funeral director. A relative supplies the particulars, and the funeral director lodges the statement of death with the municipal clerk as division registrar, who registers it and issues the burial permit required before disposal. Paper then goes to the Registrar General, and central registration can take up to 12 weeks. Public institutions, including federal ones, can receive periodic death data under s. 48.13, which is how deaths reach the SIN program and the CRA. Families still cancel Ontario cards and licences themselves.

steps.title: Death is recognised by the attending doctor, or by emergency services
steps.who: For an expected death, the doctor who was caring for the person; for an unexpected death, emergency services (paramedics), who may treat a person as dead on a completed medical certificate of death or where the person is obviously dead; where neither is available, the coroner.
steps.summary: No Ontario statute says who may pronounce death. Pronouncing death is not among the controlled acts the Regulated Health Professions Act reserves, the Vital Statistics Act and Regulation 1094 govern only the medical certificate, and the only statutory determination of death is the two-physician rule for post mortem transplants. Ontario's guidance sends families to the attending doctor (expected deaths) or emergency services (unexpected); paramedics act under the Ambulance Act regulation, which lets a crew rely on a completed medical certificate of death or on the person being obviously dead, and under Ministry patient care standards not read here.

steps.title: Report a reportable death to a coroner or police
steps.who: Every person with reason to believe the death was violent, by misadventure, negligence, misconduct or malpractice, by unfair means, pregnancy-related, sudden and unexpected, from untreated disease, from a cause other than disease, or needing investigation. Police notified must pass it to the coroner.
steps.trigger: Reason to believe the death is reportable.
steps.summary: Anyone who suspects a death is reportable must immediately notify a coroner or the police, and the police must immediately tell the coroner. For such a death, registration documentation cannot issue until the coroner has examined the body and investigated.

steps.title: Complete and deliver the medical certificate of death
steps.who: The physician or nurse practitioner in attendance during the last illness, or a registered nurse (general certificate) for an expected death meeting the listed conditions, or the coroner or nurse investigator after a coroner's investigation.

deadline.text: immediately after the death (coroner: as soon as the cause is known)

steps.summary: The certifier completes the medical certificate of death immediately after the death and delivers it to the funeral director. Under amendments made in 2022 and 2024, a registered nurse may certify an expected death from a diagnosed terminal illness. In coroner cases a warrant to bury can stand in until the cause is known.

steps.title: Informant gives personal particulars to the funeral director
steps.who: On the funeral director's request: the nearest relative present at the death or last illness, or any available relative; otherwise the occupier or an adult resident; otherwise an adult present or with knowledge; or the coroner.
steps.summary: Ontario's statutory informant duty runs to the funeral director rather than to a registrar. The relative (or next person in the regulation's order) provides and certifies the deceased's personal particulars.

steps.title: Funeral director delivers the statement of death to the division registrar
steps.who: The funeral director, to the division registrar (the municipal clerk) of the division where the death occurred or the body was found.
steps.trigger: Receipt of the particulars and of the medical certificate or warrant to bury.

deadline.text: no fixed period; the division registrar may register only within one year of death

steps.summary: The funeral director completes and certifies the statement of death and delivers it, with the medical certificate, to the municipal clerk acting as division registrar. Failure to furnish required documentation is an offence (up to $50,000 for an individual, $250,000 for a corporation).

steps.title: Division registrar registers and issues the burial permit
steps.trigger: Receipt of correct and sufficient documents within one year.
steps.summary: The division registrar registers the death by signing the documents, then issues an acknowledgment of registration and a burial permit without charge. Registration gates disposal: no burial, cremation or removal from the division without the permit, and a cemetery or crematorium may not accept a body without it.

steps.title: Division registrar forwards the registration to the Registrar General
steps.who: The division registrar, to the Office of the Registrar General (ServiceOntario).
steps.summary: After issuing the burial permit the clerk forwards the statement of death and the medical certificate (or warrant to bury) to the Registrar General. Ontario says it can take up to 12 weeks from receipt for the death to be registered centrally, which delays certificates.

steps.title: Registrar General issues death certificates and certified copies
steps.who: Death certificate: any person, on application and fee. Certified copy of the registration: only a person the Registrar General authorizes, or by court order.
steps.summary: Any person may order an Ontario death certificate. It shows only name, age, marital status, date and place of death, sex, and the registration date and number. The certified copy of the full registration is restricted. Funeral directors also issue their own proof-of-death statements for some uses.

steps.title: Registrar General discloses death data to public institutions
steps.who: The Registrar General, to an 'institution': a provincial or municipal institution under FIPPA/MFIPPA, a federal government institution under the Privacy Act, or a designated body; under an agreement and for a fee.
steps.trigger: An approved application; may be ongoing or periodic.
steps.latencyNote: ongoing or periodic; "frequency, method and timing" set by agreement (on-reg1094-s72-1-3)
steps.summary: Public institutions, including federal ones, may apply for death-certificate particulars of everyone who died in a period or a defined class, on an ongoing basis, under an agreement limiting use and onward disclosure. This is the provincial authority under which Ontario deaths reach federal programs.

steps.title: Ontario vital statistics notifies the federal SIN program
steps.who: ServiceOntario's Office of the Registrar General, to ESDC's Social Insurance Register (see ca-federal).
steps.latencyNote: "frequency, method and timing" set by agreement (on-reg1094-s72-1-3)
steps.summary: Because Ontario is a province, ESDC's statement that provincial vital statistics agencies notify the SIN program automatically applies. Ontario joined the direct death feed to the CRA in December 2013 (see ca-federal).

steps.title: Elections Ontario removes deceased electors
steps.who: The Chief Electoral Officer of Ontario, drawing on the Government of Ontario and its agencies or any reliable source; or on evidence of death given to a returning officer.
steps.trigger: Periodic updating of the permanent register, or evidence of a death.
steps.summary: The Act lets the Chief Electoral Officer update the permanent register from any reliable source, including Ontario government agencies. A deceased elector is deleted when satisfactory evidence of the death is given. Whether the Registrar General sends a regular death feed was not confirmed.

steps.title: Registrar General classifies and publishes death statistics
steps.summary: Every registered death is classified by cause under the adopted disease classification. The Registrar General publishes statistical information and an annual report on registered deaths.

steps.title: Family cancels the driver's licence and health card at ServiceOntario
steps.who: Family, next of kin or the estate.
steps.summary: Ontario's guidance tells the family to cancel the driver's licence at ServiceOntario (in person or by mail), with a death certificate or a police, court or lawyer notice of death, and to return an accessible parking permit within 30 days. No automatic cancellation from the death registration was found.

steps.title: Executor informs banks and financial institutions
steps.summary: Ontario's guidance tells the executor to inform the deceased's banks and financial institutions. The Registrar General's bulk disclosure is open only to public institutions, so private bodies have no official death-data route.

steps.title: Estate trustee advertises for creditors
steps.summary: Ontario has no statutory public notice of death. A personal representative who gives the kind of notices a court would have ordered may distribute the estate and is protected against claims not then known. In practice this is a newspaper advertisement for creditors.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: No day count for the informant or funeral director. The certificate is due 'immediately', and disposal requires the burial permit that registration produces. The division registrar can register only within one year. Central registration can take up to 12 weeks.

informantDuty.note: A relative (then occupier or other adult, then coroner) supplies the particulars to the funeral director. The funeral director completes the statement of death and delivers it to the division registrar.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of attending-practitioner certificates; coroner involvement depends on the s. 10 reporting duty.

electronicRegistration.note: The regulation provides electronic submission for birth notices, not deaths. The funeral director carries the paper statement and medical certificate to the municipal clerk.

centralPopulationRegister.note: No population register; the Registrar General holds the vital statistics registrations.

governmentPropagation.note: Federal: provincial deaths reach the SIN program and the CRA automatically, under s. 48.13 periodic disclosure. Provincial: the family must still cancel the driver's licence and health card at ServiceOntario. Elections Ontario may use government sources.

certificateAccess.note: Any person may obtain a death certificate with limited particulars. Certified copies of the registration go only to persons the Registrar General authorizes or by court order.

privateSectorVerification.note: Bulk death disclosure under s. 48.13 is limited to public 'institutions' (FIPPA, MFIPPA, federal Privacy Act bodies, designated bodies). Banks and insurers rely on the estate's certificate.

gaps: Pronouncement: the Ministry of Health's Basic Life Support Patient Care Standards (incorporated by O. Reg. 257/00 s. 11), which set paramedic rules for deceased patients, and College of Nurses / CPSO practice standards on pronouncement were not read (cpso.on.ca and cno.org are egress-denied). The pronounce step records the statutory silence and the guidance only.

Ontario's 'integrated notifications' to federal programs: no ServiceOntario page was found saying registration notifies federal programs. The link rests on VSA s. 48.13, on ESDC's statement that provinces notify the SIN program, and on the 2014 Ombudsperson report that Ontario joined the CRA feed in December 2013 (see ca-federal).

Whether OHIP (health insurance) and the Ministry of Transportation (driver's licences) receive an automatic death feed from the Registrar General was not established. Ontario's own guidance tells families to cancel licences and return permits.
Whether Elections Ontario receives a regular death list from the Registrar General (as BC's does by statute) was not confirmed; the Election Act only authorizes reliable government sources.
The Funeral, Burial and Cremation Services Act, 2002 and O. Reg. 30/11 were not mined for cremation-specific waiting periods or coroner cremation certificates.
Electronic death registration: no provision for electronic death submission was found in Reg. 1094. Any administrative e-registration pilot was not searched for.
